blinding_guess.why: The RAII constructor api:ecl::Serial::Serial initialises only port, read_timeout_ms and error_handler (serial_pos.cpp:52), not is_open or file_descriptor, then calls open(...), whose first step if (open()) close(); reads the uninitialised is_open and can ::close an uninitialised descriptor. Also the default constructor (serial_pos.hpp:144) leaves read_timeout_ms uninitialised, so open(...) calls block(read_timeout_ms) with an indeterminate timeout, although the doc promises a 5 s default (serial_pos.hpp:198-199).

notes: The snapshot is the whole ecl_core repository; the package is snapshot/ecl_devices. serial.hpp selects serial_pos.hpp under ECL_IS_POSIX and serial_w32.hpp under ECL_IS_WIN32; ros_distro is hydro (Linux), so declarations are recorded from the POSIX header. Each packet element has several overloads, and one representative is recorded per element: Serial::Serial = the parameterised RAII constructor (the other is the inline default constructor Serial() : is_open(false), error_handler(NoError) {}; at serial_pos.hpp:144); Serial::open = the parameterised overload (the other is the status accessor bool open(); at serial_pos.hpp:230); Serial::read and Serial::write = the buffer templates with (bytes, n) (single-byte templates long read(Byte &byte) at serial_pos.hpp:324 and long write(const Byte &byte) at serial_pos.hpp:245 also exist). Multi-line declarations are joined with whitespace collapsed, and template headers are included. The Win32 header declares different signatures for the same symbols: void open(...) throws instead of returning bool (serial_w32.hpp:173), void block(const long &timeout = 500) ecl_assert_throw_decl(StandardException); (serial_w32.hpp:234), and non-template char-based long read(char *s, const unsigned long &n) and long write(const char *s, unsigned long n) (serial_w32.hpp:212, 276). block(): timeouts below 100 ms use an internal polling loop (1/2/5 ms periods); at 100 ms or more it sets termios VTIME = timeout/100 (serial_pos.cpp:271-323). On the lock-failure path, open() uses the ecl_throw_decl(...) macro instead of ecl_throw (serial_pos.cpp:129); with exceptions enabled this expands to throw(...) (ecl_exceptions macros.hpp:64), and the descriptor is not closed. The exclusive resource is the device named at run time by port_name. It is locked with fcntl F_WRLCK on POSIX; on Win32 CreateFileA is called with share mode 0 (serial_w32.cpp:88-90). No ROS topics, services, messages or parameters are involved, so QoS, rate and definition_id are null. definition_hash.py was not needed. There are no consumed packet elements, so references is empty.
